answers.quote: According to tradition and epigraphic evidence two brothers, Harihara and Bukka, founded the Vijayanagara Empire in 1336.
answers.notes: Founded by Harihara and Bukka in 1336 per tradition/epigraphic evidence.

answers.quote: While historians use the term Vijayanagara Empire, contemporaries described it as the karnataka samrajyamu.
answers.notes: Contemporaries described it as karnataka samrajyamu.

answers.answer: আলাউদ্দিন বাহমান শাহ (হাসান গাঙ্গু / জাফর খান)
answers.quote: Zafar Khan could easily defeat the imperial army and the new king Nasir-ud-din readily abdicated the throne in favour of Zafar Khan who proclaimed himself sultan under the title Alauddin Bahman Shah. This was the beginning of the Bahmani line of Kings.
answers.notes: Zafar Khan (Hasan Gangu) proclaimed himself Alauddin Bahman Shah.

answers.quote: Krishnadeva Raya (ruled 1509-29), the most famous ruler of Vijayanagara, composed a work on statecraft in Telugu known as the Amuktamalyada. Krishnadeva Raya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.
answers.notes: Krishnadeva Raya composed Amuktamalyada.

answers.quote: Krishnadeva Raya (ruled 1509-29), the most famous ruler of Vijayanagara, composed a work on statecraft in Telugu known as the Amuktamalyada. Krishnadeva Raya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.
answers.notes: Krishnadeva Raya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.

answers.quote: The ruins at Hampi were brought to light in 1800 by an engineer and antiquarian named Colonel Colin Mackenzie. he prepared the first survey map of the site.
answers.notes: Ruins brought to light in 1800 by Colonel Colin Mackenzie.

answers.answer: দুর্গ নিয়ন্ত্রণকারী ও সশস্ত্র অনুগামীসম্পন্ন সামরিক প্রধানদের
answers.quote: These chiefs were known as nayakas and they usually spoke Telugu or Kannada.
answers.notes: Nayakas were military chiefs controlling forts with armed supporters.

answers.quote: In 1565 Rama Raya, the chief minister of Vijayanagara, led the army into battle at Rakshasi-Tangadi (also known as Talikota), where his forces were routed by the combined armies of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda.
answers.notes: In 1565 Rama Raya led the army at Talikota.

answers.quote: The most striking feature about the location of Vijayanagara is the natural basin formed by the river Tungabhadra which flows in a north-easterly direction. The surrounding landscape is characterised by stunning granite hills that seem to form a girdle around the city.
answers.notes: City in natural basin formed by river Tungabhadra.

answers.quote: The kingdom originated due to the revolt of the amirs of the Delhi Sultanate.
answers.notes: Bahmani kingdom originated due to revolt of the amirs of Delhi Sultanate.

answers.quote: The first dynasty, known as the Sangama dynasty, exercised control till 1485. They were supplanted by the Saluvas, military commanders, who remained in power till 1503 when they were replaced by the Tuluvas.
answers.notes: Sangama till 1485, supplanted by Saluvas.

answers.answer: বুক্ক, হরিহর, কম্পন, মুদাপ্পা ও মারাপ্পা
answers.quote: The foundation of the Vijayanagara state towards the middle of the 14th century is generally attributed to a group of five brothers, namely, Bukka, Harihara, Kampana, Mudappa and Marappa. The founding figures of the kingdom are also known as the Sangamas, after their father's name.
answers.notes: Five brothers: Bukka, Harihara, Kampana, Mudappa and Marappa.

answers.quote: This was the time when the land between the Tungabhadra and Krishna rivers (the Raichur doab) was acquired (1512), the rulers of Orissa were subdued (1514) and severe defeats were inflicted on the Sultan of Bijapur (1520).
answers.notes: Raichur doab acquired in 1512.

answers.quote: Krishnadeva Raya is credited with building some fine temples and adding impressive gopurams to many important south Indian temples. He also founded a suburban township near Vijayanagara called Nagalapuram after his mother.
answers.notes: Founded suburban township Nagalapuram after his mother.

answers.quote: The amara-nayaka system was a major political innovation of the Vijayanagara Empire. It is likely that many features of this system were derived from the iqta system of the Delhi Sultanate.
answers.notes: Features likely derived from iqta system of Delhi Sultanate.

answers.answer: বার্ষিক আর্থিক অর্থ রাজকোষে জমা দেওয়া এবং রাজার জন্য সৈন্য রাখা ও তাঁর যুদ্ধে সেবা করা
answers.quote: In return the Nayakas had twofold duties: 1) remitting an annual financial contribution to the imperial exchequer, and 2) maintaining for the king a sufficient number of troops and serving him in his wars.
answers.notes: Twofold duties: annual contribution and maintaining troops/serving in wars.

answers.quote: Nayakas held land in the form of military fief known as amaram tenure.
answers.notes: Nayakas held land as military fief known as amaram tenure.

answers.quote: Abdur Razzaq, an ambassador sent by the ruler of Persia to Calicut (present-day Kozhikode) in the fifteenth century, was greatly impressed by the fortifications, and mentioned seven lines of forts. These encircled not only the city but also its agricultural hinterland and forests.
answers.notes: Abdur Razzaq mentioned seven lines of forts.

answers.quote: The most important such tank was built in the early years of the fifteenth century and is now called Kamalapuram tank. Water from this tank not only irrigated fields nearby but was also conducted through a channel to the “royal centre”.
answers.notes: Kamalapuram tank water conducted through channel to royal centre.

answers.quote: One of the most prominent waterworks to be seen among the ruins is the Hiriya canal. This canal drew water from a dam across the Tungabhadra and irrigated the cultivated valley that separated the “sacred centre” from the “urban core”. This was apparently built by kings of the Sangama dynasty.
answers.notes: Hiriya canal irrigated valley between sacred centre and urban core.

answers.quote: Located on one of the highest points in the city, the “mahanavami dibba” is a massive platform rising from a base of about 11,000 sq. ft to a height of 40 ft.
answers.notes: Base about 11,000 sq ft, height 40 ft.

answers.answer: দেবতা বিরূপাক্ষের পক্ষে; 'শ্রী বিরূপাক্ষ' নামে স্বাক্ষর
answers.quote: In fact the Vijayanagara kings claimed to rule on behalf of the god Virupaksha. All royal orders were signed “Shri Virupaksha”, usually in the Kannada script.
answers.notes: Kings claimed to rule on behalf of Virupaksha; orders signed Shri Virupaksha.

answers.quote: These Muslim groups were the Deccanis who were the descendants of the Muslims who had been staying in India for a long time and the Paradesis who were foreigners who had recently arrived. The Deccanis were mainly the Sunnis whereas the Paradesis belonged to the Shiah sect and this aggravated their rivalry.
answers.notes: Nobility divided between Deccanis and Paradesis.

answers.quote: According to some historians, Bahmani kingdom enjoyed its glory in the period from 1461 to 1481 when Mahmud Gawan was the prime minister.
answers.notes: Glory period 1461-1481 when Mahmud Gawan was prime minister.

answers.quote: Strain began to show within the imperial structure following Krishnadeva Raya's death in 1529. By 1542 control at the centre had shifted to another ruling lineage, that of the Aravidu, which remained in power till the end of the seventeenth century.
answers.notes: By 1542 control shifted to Aravidu lineage.

answers.answer: উর্বর নদী-উপত্যকার নিয়ন্ত্রণ এবং লাভজনক সমুদ্র-বাণিজ্যের সম্পদ
answers.quote: On their northern frontier, the Vijayanagara kings competed with contemporary rulers – including the Sultans of the Deccan and the Gajapati rulers of Orissa – for control of the fertile river valleys and the resources generated by lucrative overseas trade.
answers.notes: Competition for fertile river valleys and resources of lucrative overseas trade.

answers.answer: প্রথাগত এক-ষষ্ঠাংশ থেকে মোট উৎপাদনের অর্ধেক পর্যন্ত
answers.quote: Nilakanta Sasthri observes that the proportion of produce claimed as revenue varied from the traditional one sixth to as much as half the gross yield.
answers.notes: Revenue varied from traditional one-sixth to half the gross yield.

answers.answer: প্রতি বছর রাজস্ব-উপহার (tribute) পাঠিয়ে এবং উপহারসহ নিজে রাজদরবারে উপস্থিত হয়ে
answers.quote: The amara-nayakas sent tribute to the king annually and personally appeared in the royal court with gifts to express their loyalty. Kings occasionally asserted their control over them by transferring them from one place to another.
answers.notes: Sent tribute annually and personally appeared in court with gifts.

answers.answer: মধ্যযুগীয় অবরোধে শত্রু রক্ষীদের অনাহারে আত্মসমর্পণে বাধ্য করত; কৃষি-বলয় সুরক্ষিত থাকলে দীর্ঘ অবরোধেও খাদ্য জোগান থাকত
answers.quote: Often, the objective of medieval sieges was to starve the defenders into submission. The rulers of Vijayanagara adopted a more expensive and elaborate strategy of protecting the agricultural belt itself.
answers.notes: Sieges aimed to starve defenders; strategy protected agricultural belt itself.

answers.quote: Rulers also indicated their close links with the gods by using the title “Hindu Suratrana”. This was a Sanskritisation of the Arabic term Sultan, meaning king, so it literally meant Hindu Sultan.
answers.notes: Hindu Suratrana literally meant Hindu Sultan.

answers.answer: প্রধান দেবতা বিট্ঠল (মহারাষ্ট্রে পূজিত বিষ্ণুর রূপ) এবং রথের আকারে নির্মিত অনন্য গর্ভগৃহ
answers.quote: Here, the principal deity was Vitthala, a form of Vishnu generally worshipped in Maharashtra. As in the case of other temples, this temple too has several halls and a unique shrine designed as a chariot (Fig. 7.24).
answers.notes: Principal deity Vitthala, form of Vishnu worshipped in Maharashtra; unique shrine as chariot.

answers.answer: জাল চিঠির অভিযোগে সুলতান তাঁর শিরশ্ছেদের আদেশ দেন
answers.quote: Inspite of Gawan’s explanations he was ordered to be beheaded and the order was executed immediately. This was the beginning of the end of the Bahmani kingdom.
answers.notes: Gawan ordered beheaded despite explanations; claim states forged-letter charge; beginning of the end.

answers.answer: ১৪৭০–৭৪, চার বছর; অভিজাতদের বিলাসিতা বনাম সাধারণ মানুষের দারিদ্র্যের তীব্র বৈপরীত্য
answers.quote: It was during the lifetime of Mahmud Gawan that the Russian merchant Athanasius Nikitin visited Bidar. Nikitin was in Bidar for four years from 1470-74. He has emphasised the great contrast between the huge wealth and luxury of the nobility and the miserable poverty of the common people in the countryside.
answers.notes: Nikitin in Bidar four years 1470-74; contrast luxury of nobility vs poverty of common people.

answers.answer: এক সুলতানকে অন্যের বিরুদ্ধে খেলানোর দুঃসাহসিক নীতি
answers.quote: It was the adventurous policy of Rama Raya who tried to play off one Sultan against another that led the Sultans to combine together and decisively defeat him.
answers.notes: Adventurous policy of playing off one Sultan against another led Sultans to combine.

answers.answer: অনেক নায়ক স্বাধীন রাজ্য প্রতিষ্ঠা করায়
answers.quote: However, during the course of the seventeenth century, many of these nayakas established independent kingdoms. This hastened the collapse of the central imperial structure.
answers.notes: Many nayakas established independent kingdoms, hastening collapse.

answers.quote: While historians use the term Vijayanagara Empire, contemporaries described it as the karnataka samrajyamu.
answers.notes: Both statements supported: c05 for statement 1 and c04 for statement 2 (1336, Harihara and Bukka). Quote given is for statement 1; see notes.

answers.quote: The amara-nayakas were military commanders who were given territories to govern by the raya. They collected taxes and other dues from peasants, craftspersons and traders in the area. They retained part of the revenue for personal use and for maintaining a stipulated contingent of horses and elephants.
answers.notes: Both supported by c19: collected taxes from peasants/craftspersons/traders and retained revenue for stipulated horses/elephants contingent.

answers.quote: Krishnadeva Raya (ruled 1509-29), the most famous ruler of Vijayanagara, composed a work on statecraft in Telugu known as the Amuktamalyada. Krishnadeva Raya belonged to the Tuluva dynasty.
answers.notes: A Krishnadeva-Amuktamalyada c11; B Rama Raya-Talikota c15; C Mackenzie survey c03; D Gawan PM 1461-81 c53.

answers.quote: The first dynasty, known as the Sangama dynasty, exercised control till 1485. They were supplanted by the Saluvas, military commanders, who remained in power till 1503 when they were replaced by the Tuluvas.
answers.notes: Order Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, Aravidu from c10 and c14.

answers.answer: A ও R দুটোই সঠিক এবং R হল A-এর সঠিক ব্যাখ্যা
answers.quote: Inspite of Gawan’s explanations he was ordered to be beheaded and the order was executed immediately. This was the beginning of the end of the Bahmani kingdom.
answers.notes: A from c55 (beginning of the end); R from c54 (able administrator, survey and assessment reforms).

answers.quote: One of the most beautiful buildings in the royal centre is the Lotus Mahal, so named by British travellers in the nineteenth century. One suggestion, found in a map drawn by Mackenzie, is that it may have been a council chamber, a place where the king met his advisers.
answers.notes: Pairs 1-3 supported by c23, c31, c36; pair 4 is wrong: Lotus Mahal is a royal-centre building, suggested council chamber (c30), not a temple built by Krishnadeva Raya.

answers.quote: In 1565 Rama Raya, the chief minister of Vijayanagara, led the army into battle at Rakshasi-Tangadi (also known as Talikota), where his forces were routed by the combined armies of Bijapur, Ahmadnagar and Golconda.
answers.notes: Statement 1 from c15 (1565, combined Bijapur/Ahmadnagar/Golconda routed Rama Raya); statement 2 from c02 (city sacked in 1565 and subsequently deserted).
